jobs.objective: REVISE the RFC 0165 implementation SPEC (Claude provider credential freshness + spawn-time hydration, #583) to DISCHARGE the two binding v1 findings, carrying forward UNREGRESSED everything v1 got right. Read the v3 SEED, RFC 0165, the v1 HOLDER.md (the base — revise it, do NOT rewrite from scratch), and the v1 cycle-1 collaboration ledger (its findings F1/F2 + constraints are the exact prescribed fixes) first. Do NOT rely on any rfc-0165-design-v2 artifact (quarantined). The host cred-resync timer (#583, live) is the STATUS QUO this RFC replaces — do NOT propose 'the host timer handles it'. DISCHARGE F2 (no lane raw-refresh-token custody, CRITICAL): the v1 JIT file-copy model (~striatum-lane/.claude/.credentials.json) gives each lane raw refresh-token custody; with OAuth refresh-token rotation a lane-side refresh rotates the token in the lane file while the operator source stays stale, INVALIDATING the operator source for future lanes and possibly the operator's own CLI, and concurrent lanes share stale copied refresh-token state. FIX: move to a daemon-managed credential broker / access-token model (or an equally concrete, equally explicit OAuth-safe design) where lanes do NOT receive raw refresh tokens and CANNOT independently rotate the operator credential family — the lane receives only what it needs to make Claude calls (a short-lived access token or a brokered read), refresh authority held in exactly one place; prove no operator-source corruption and no concurrent/subsequent-lane desync; add named concurrent-lane and subsequent-lane refresh-token-rotation (RTR) tests. DISCHARGE F1 (runtime-expiry circuit breaker, HIGH): spawn-time hydration can pass then the credential expires mid-session before first Claude use; the stored dependency/receipt still say ready/passed so recovery treats the agent_mcp_discovery_stall as GENERIC and burns requeue/transfer budget before reseed_required is found later. FIX: recovery must perform a CURRENT freshness check (against the lane credential or an equivalent daemon-owned provider-auth state) BEFORE incrementing generic requeue/transfer counters, and the supervisor/heartbeat path must report provider credential expiry/near-expiry as provider-auth READINESS DEBT before ordinary stall recovery fires. CARRY FORWARD UNREGRESSED: the spawn-time freshness gate (no stale/expired/unparseable/generation-drifted launch on every spawn/respawn/recovery requeue), the RFC 0096/#135/#296 trust boundary (provider OAuth separate from Striatum session-bound tokens; lanes never get daemon/admin tokens or mint authority), provider_auth_gate=off cannot bypass hydration, and redacted private-safe custody receipts (no raw OAuth in DB/artifacts/metrics/events/doctor). ANCHOR fixes to real source: the lane-launch/hydration path (go/pkg/supervisor), the recovery decision tree, the heartbeat/supervisor path, the RFC 0162 expiry telemetry. State each constraint as a FALSIFIABLE assertion + its test. Open the SPEC with an auditable 'Addressing the v1 findings' map (F2 RESOLVED how, F1 RESOLVED how, carry-forwards INTACT). This is the published claim the falsifiers re-attack.
jobs.title: Hold leading proposal

jobs.objective: Read the published REVISED (v3) holder SPEC, the v1 HOLDER.md, and the v1 cycle-1 ledger (its F1 finding). Your lens is F1 / RUNTIME-EXPIRY + RECOVERY-CLASSIFICATION. FIRST verify F1 is GENUINELY resolved: does recovery now classify runtime credential expiry as provider-auth readiness debt BEFORE consuming generic requeue/transfer budget? Does the heartbeat/supervisor path surface provider credential expiry or near-expiry as provider-auth debt before ordinary stall recovery fires? Construct the launch-fresh-then-expire-mid-session case (lane launches with 35min freshness, works 45min locally, expires before its first model/MCP action, enters agent_mcp_discovery_stall): is it now CAUGHT as provider-auth debt, or does it STILL leak into generic MCP-discovery recovery and burn budget? Is the freshness check itself cheap and race-free (no TOCTOU between check and use)? Then hunt NEW gaps: does the recovery-time check have a window where a just-expired credential still passes? Does near-expiry classification flap? If runtime expiry still leaks to generic recovery, the check is racy, or a new material gap stands, say so explicitly and stop the gate from clearing.
jobs.title: Falsifier 1

jobs.objective: Read the published REVISED (v3) holder SPEC, the v1 HOLDER.md, and the v1 cycle-1 ledger (its F2 finding). Your lens is F2 / CREDENTIAL-CUSTODY + OAUTH-SAFETY + CARRY-FORWARD REGRESSION. FIRST verify F2 is GENUINELY resolved: can a lane still obtain raw refresh-token custody by ANY route (a residual file copy, a leaked env var, a broker that hands back the refresh token, a readable store)? Can a lane-side refresh still rotate or invalidate the OPERATOR SOURCE credential family? Build the concurrent-lane RTR case (two lanes refresh near-simultaneously) and the subsequent-lane case (lane A refreshes, lane B launches later) — do they desynchronize or invalidate the source? Does the broker/access-token model keep provider OAuth SEPARATE from Striatum control-plane tokens (no daemon/admin authority or mint capability leaked to lanes, RFC 0096/#135/#296)? Is any raw OAuth material exposed in DB rows / repo artifacts / metrics / events / doctor output? THEN spend the rest on REGRESSION — verify each carry-forward survives: the spawn-time freshness gate (every spawn/respawn/recovery requeue), the trust boundary, provider_auth_gate=off cannot bypass hydration, redacted custody receipts. Confirm the F1 recovery-classification change did not perturb the custody model. If a lane can still hold or rotate a raw refresh token, the operator source can be invalidated, OAuth leaks, or any carry-forward regressed, say so explicitly and stop the gate from clearing.
jobs.title: Falsifier 2

jobs.objective: Read only the dialogue trajectory for the RFC 0165 v3 REVISION (the revised HOLDER.md and the two FALSIFIER.md challenges), with the v1 HOLDER.md and the v1 cycle-1 ledger (its F1/F2 findings) as context for what the revision had to fix. Publish the collaboration ledger verdict (accept / accept_with_findings / needs_revision / reject — a clearing verdict is accept or accept_with_findings, never `clear`). A clearing verdict REQUIRES BOTH: F2 GENUINELY DISCHARGED — lanes never receive raw refresh-token custody and cannot rotate/invalidate the operator source credential family (a daemon-managed broker / access-token model or an equally concrete OAuth-safe design); the concurrent-lane and subsequent-lane RTR tests are specified; provider OAuth stays separate from Striatum control-plane tokens; no raw OAuth material leaks to DB/artifacts/metrics/events/doctor; AND F1 GENUINELY DISCHARGED — recovery classifies runtime credential expiry as provider-auth readiness debt BEFORE consuming generic requeue/transfer budget, and the heartbeat/supervisor path surfaces expiry/near-expiry as readiness debt, with the launch-fresh-then-expire-mid-session test specified and the freshness check race-free; AND no carry-forward regressed (spawn-time gate, trust boundary, provider_auth_gate=off cannot bypass, redacted custody receipts); AND no new material challenge stands unrebutted. Record per finding F1/F2 whether RESOLVED, per carry-forward whether INTACT, per new challenge whether it stands. needs_revision if either finding remains open (lane can hold/rotate a raw refresh token / operator source invalidatable / runtime expiry still leaks to generic recovery), if any carry-forward regressed, or if a new material challenge lands. This is the single allowed v3 revision cycle; a second needs_revision ends the gate unCleared and routes to the operator (who spins a fresh -v4 run with a revising holder).
jobs.title: Adjudicate dialogue substance

jobs.objective: Publish the cleared, revised falsifiable RFC 0165 implementation SPEC — ONLY after the adjudicator ledger records a clearing verdict — consolidating the WHOLE design (not just the F1/F2 deltas), buildable contract-first by the rfc-0165-build code_change run: the daemon-managed credential broker / access-token model (lanes never hold raw refresh tokens; refresh authority in one place; F2), the recovery-time + heartbeat freshness classification routing runtime expiry to provider-auth readiness debt (F1), the spawn-time freshness gate on every spawn/respawn/recovery requeue, the RFC 0096/#135/#296 trust boundary (provider OAuth separate from session-bound control-plane tokens), provider_auth_gate=off cannot bypass, and the redacted private-safe custody receipts. State each as a falsifiable assertion + its test (the concurrent-lane and subsequent-lane RTR tests, the launch-fresh-then-expire-mid-session recovery test, the spawn-time gate test, the trust-boundary control, the no-raw-OAuth-leak control). Anchor to source (the supervisor lane-launch/hydration path, the recovery decision tree, the heartbeat path, RFC 0162 expiry telemetry). Note the seams for later slices. Reference the clearing ledger. This consolidated SPEC is the single source the build run implements.
